stem:
Aditi observes a sample. It is shiny, can be hammered into a thin sheet, can be drawn into a wire, and rings when struck. It also feels hard compared with chalk.

Which decision about these observations is correct?

options.text: Lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility and sonority are used here as metal tests, so the sample is likely a metal.
Only shininess matters; hardness, malleability, ductility and sonority are not used as metal tests.
These observations show the sample must be a non-metal.
Malleability and ductility are used only for non-metals, not for metals.

teacher.key_rationale: Lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility and sonority are the usual metal tests on an observed sample.
